LESSON: RESPONSIBILITY VALUES

Grade: Grade 2
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Christian 4.5 By the end of the Sub strand, the learner ● Learners to read Luke 
Topic 4.6: Responsibility Values

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Responsibility Values. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain Responsibility Values in simple words
2. give Kenyan school/community examples of Responsibility Values
3. describe one responsible action linked to Responsibility Values
4. show respect and fairness when practising Responsibility Values

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: RESPONSIBILITY VALUES
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Responsibility Values helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: RESPONSIBILITY VALUES
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Explain Responsibility Values in simple words

What this means
In this part you learn to explain Responsibility Values in simple words. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain Responsibility Values in simple words.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Responsibility Values” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain Responsibility Values in simple words. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Give Kenyan school/community examples of Responsibility Values

What this means
In this part you learn to give Kenyan school/community examples of Responsibility Values. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: give Kenyan school/community examples of Responsibility Values.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Responsibility Values in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can give Kenyan school/community examples of Responsibility Values. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Describe one responsible action linked to Responsibility Values

What this means
In this part you learn to describe one responsible action linked to Responsibility Values. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe one responsible action linked to Responsibility Values.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe one responsible action linked to Responsibility Values. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Show respect and fairness when practising Responsibility Values

What this means
In this part you learn to show respect and fairness when practising Responsibility Values. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: show respect and fairness when practising Responsibility Values.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Responsibility Values” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can show respect and fairness when practising Responsibility Values. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Responsibility Values is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Show how “Responsibility Values” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: explain Responsibility Values in simple words)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Responsibility Values in your own words. (skill: give Kenyan school/community examples of Responsibility Values)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: describe one responsible action linked to Responsibility Values)

Example 4: Show how “Responsibility Values” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: show respect and fairness when practising Responsibility Values)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Responsibility Values to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain Responsibility Values in simple words.
3. Practise this skill: give Kenyan school/community examples of Responsibility Values.
4. Practise this skill: describe one responsible action linked to Responsibility Values.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Responsibility Values from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Responsibility Values: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 2 learner study Responsibility Values?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Responsibility Values means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain Responsibility Values in simple words.
5. Be able to: give Kenyan school/community examples of Responsibility Values.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
